author: Great Lakes Wire
title: Dearborn Heights to honor retiring Fire Chief David Brogan at June 1 open house
text:
The City of Dearborn Heights will host a retirement celebration for Fire Chief David Brogan on June 1 at the Dearborn Heights Fire Department Headquarters. The event, scheduled from 11:00 AM to 2:00 PM, is open to the public, city employees, elected officials, representatives from neighboring communities, members of the Michigan Chiefs Association, and members of the media.
The celebration will include remarks from city leadership and a reception lunch. Attendees are invited to stop by during the open house to recognize Chief Brogan’s service to Dearborn Heights.
Chief Brogan began his career with the Dearborn Heights Fire Department in February 1992 and has served in roles ranging from Firefighter up through Pump Operator, Lieutenant, Captain, and Fire Marshal before becoming Chief. He was one of nine original paramedics when advanced life support services were introduced in the department.
Brogan also held elected positions within the Dearborn Heights Professional Firefighters Union Local 1355 and completed Eastern Michigan University’s School of Staff and Command in October 2013. He is a member of both the National Fire Protection Association and International Association of Fire Chiefs. His family has deep roots in fire service; his father retired as Senior Chief after nearly four decades with Detroit’s fire department.
“Chief Brogan’s commitment to this city and its residents has left a lasting mark on our Fire Department and on Dearborn Heights as a whole. It is only fitting that we honor his legacy by naming our new fire station after him, ensuring that his name stands as a symbol of service and dedication for generations to come,” said Mayor Mo Baydoun. “This celebration is a reflection of the deep respect our community has for his service.”
